metaDescription: Learn the core mechanics of OpenThrone: races, turns, combat, economy, and alliances. Your guide to dominating the realm.

hero.title: How to Play
hero.subtitle: Master the core loop. Turns generate over time. Spend them wisely to attack, plunder, and climb the ranks.

coreLoop.title: The Core Loop
coreLoop.description: OpenThrone runs on a persistent cycle. Every {{minutes}} minutes you earn attack turns. Spend turns to raid other players for gold and experience. Use gold to grow your army and fortify your kingdom. Rise through the ranks until your name is whispered across the realm.

earn.title: Earn Turns
earn.text: Attack turns regenerate every {{minutes}} minutes, even while offline.

attack.title: Attack & Plunder
attack.text: Spend turns to raid other commanders. Steal gold and earn experience.

build.title: Build & Equip
build.text: Invest gold in soldiers, weapons, armor, and fortifications.

dominate.title: Dominate
dominate.text: Climb the leaderboards. Form alliances. Control the realm.

races.title: Choose Your Race
races.description: Four distinct races, each with unique strengths. Your choice shapes your strategy from day one.

elf.name: Elf
elf.description: +5% defense bonus. Elven spies gain a 5% strength multiplier; sentries also gain 5% strength and a further 4% multiplier.

human.name: Human
human.description: +5% offense bonus, with an additional 2% multiplier to offensive, defensive, and spy strength. A flexible choice for mixed armies.

goblin.name: Goblin
goblin.description: +5% defense bonus and a 3% pillage bonus before loot caps. Build a guarded kingdom and profit from successful raids.

races.matchups: Race bonuses shape your army; no race automatically defeats another. Melee attacks meet melee defense, and ranged attacks meet ranged defense. Scout the enemy and equip troops for the pressure you expect.
races.classesDescription: Your class is the second choice at signup, and it's permanent. Each gives one lasting bonus:

army.title: Build Your Army
army.description: Citizens arrive daily. Decide how to train each one — your army composition defines your strategy.

workers.title: Workers
workers.text: Generate gold passively. The backbone of your economy.

attack.title: Attack Soldiers
attack.text: Your offensive force. Equip with weapons to maximize plunder.

defense.title: Defense Soldiers
defense.text: Protect your kingdom from raids. Equip with armor to survive sieges.

spies.title: Spies
spies.text: Scout enemy defenses before attacking. Sabotage from the shadows.

economy.title: Economy & Structures
economy.description: Gold is the lifeblood of your empire. Manage it wisely — what you don't protect, someone will take.

bank.title: Bank
bank.text: Deposit gold so raiders cannot take it. There is no limit on how much the bank holds; Economy upgrades raise how many deposits you can make each day.

armory.title: Armory
armory.text: Buy weapons and armor for your troops. Armory upgrades unlock better gear.

housing.title: Housing
housing.text: Brings new citizens to your kingdom every day. Upgrade it for more citizens; higher levels need a stronger fortification.

repair.title: Repair
repair.text: Attacks damage your fort. Spend gold here to restore its hit points.

fortifications.title: Fortifications
fortifications.text: Your fort starts as a Manor. Upgrade it under Structures > Upgrades, which opens at level 5 with the Village, for more defense, gold per turn and fort hit points.

economyUpgrades.title: Economy Upgrades
economyUpgrades.text: Also under Upgrades. Farms, markets and mines raise the gold each worker earns and how many deposits you can make each day.

combat.title: Combat & Espionage
combat.description: Victory isn't just about numbers. Scout your targets, exploit weaknesses, and time your strikes.

attack.title: Attacking
attack.text: Choose a target, commit attack turns, and plunder gold. Stronger armies deal more damage.

defense.title: Defending
defense.text: When attacked, your defense soldiers and fortifications determine your losses.

spy.title: Spy Operations
spy.text: Send spies to scout enemy troop counts before committing to an attack.

losses.title: Losses
losses.text: Casualties fall on all of your unit levels in proportion to how many troops you field at each level, so cheap level 1 troops no longer shield your best units. Mercenaries unlock from level {{mercenaryLevel}}: once your fort is a {{mercenaryFort}}, Battle → Mercenaries opens; once hired, they take the front line within their level.

protection.title: New-Player Protection
protection.text: New-player protection is a gold shield, not immunity: attacks still kill units and damage your fort. Your first {{allowance}} gold on hand is shielded — raiders take at most {{share}}% of the normal cap from it at level 1, rising to 100% at level {{taperLevel}} — and gold above that is raided at the normal rate, so bank it. Protection ends after a set number of game days, at a population threshold or at level 10, whichever comes first.

experience.title: Experience and Levels
experience.text: Experience (XP) comes from battle. Winning an attack pays the most, scaled by the turns you commit, the level gap and how close the fight was. A lost attack pays a smaller share, and only for a real fight: nothing below {{effortFloor}}% of the defender's strength, the full share from {{effortFull}}%. Defenders earn XP whenever they are attacked, more for holding than for falling, scaled by the size of the threat (at least {{threatFloor}}%). Stay on one level for more than {{graceDays}} game days and the XP you get from being attacked grows by {{stallStep}}% each further game day, up to {{stallMax}}×, so nobody can hide at a low level. Spy missions give no XP. The Overview shows how much XP your next level needs; each level gives a proficiency point and, at milestones, opens new structures.

alliances.title: Alliances
alliances.description: No commander rules alone. Join or create an alliance for mutual protection, coordinated attacks, and shared glory.
alliances.eraReserve: Alliances survive a new era. When an era ends every alliance becomes reserved: its name, roster, ranks and artwork are kept, but its treasury, loans, troop contracts and wars are closed and its features stay locked. Members can leave at any time. The leader reactivates the alliance in the new era by reaching level 10 and paying 10,000,000 gold (admins can change both).
alliances.hall: Each alliance has an Alliance Hall level, from Camp up to Stronghold. It sets how many members the alliance holds (10 at Camp, up to 100), how many times each member may deposit per 24 hours (2 at Camp, up to 8) and how much gold deposits may bring the treasury to (5,000,000 at Camp, up to 10,000,000,000). The leader, or a rank with "Buy upgrades", buys the next level with treasury gold on the alliance's Upgrades tab, which lists every level's cost, member requirement and limits. A new era returns the hall to Camp.
alliances.dues: An alliance may charge a join fee, paid once from your gold on hand when you join (up to 10,000,000 gold), and membership dues taken from every member except the leader at the start of each day, week or month (up to 1,000,000, 5,000,000 or 20,000,000 gold per member). You see both, and confirm them, before you join. Dues you cannot pay are owed and taken first at the next collection, or paid from the alliance page; nobody is removed for them. The leader, or a rank with "Set join fee and dues", sets them on the Settings tab.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.description: Settings has a Your data section: download a copy of your account and game data, or ask for your account to be erased. An erasure is confirmed by email and then waits 14 days, so you can still change your mind.
